en: The Path of Discrimination 3, Chapter on Wisdom 3.7. The Discourse on the Equal Head The Blessed One said: "Monks, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Buddha then asked: "What four? Here, monks, one person is equal in head (samasīsaka) with respect to the past, equal in head with respect to the future, equal in head with respect to the present, and equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the past? Here, monks, a certain person has already exhausted the influxes (āsava) in the past; he has already attained final knowledge (aññā); he has already realized the supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the past.

And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the future? Here, monks, a certain person will exhaust the influxes in the future; he will attain final knowledge; he will realize the supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the present? Here, monks, a certain person is exhausting the influxes in the present; he is attaining final knowledge; he is realizing the supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the present. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future? Here, monks, a certain person has already exhausted the influxes in the past and will also exhaust the influxes in the future; he has already attained final knowledge and will also attain final knowledge; he has already realized the supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna, and will also realize the supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. These, monks, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Buddha then asked: "What four? Here, monks, one person is equal in head with respect to the past, equal in head with respect to the future, equal in head with respect to the present, and equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the past? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the fetters (saṃyojana) in the past; he has already severed the underlying tendencies (anusaya); he has already destroyed the outflows (āsava). This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the past. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the future? Here, monks, a certain person will abandon the fetters in the future; he will sever the underlying tendencies; he will destroy the outflows. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the present? Here, monks, a certain person is abandoning the fetters in the present; he is severing the underlying tendencies; he is destroying the outflows. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the present. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the fetters in the past and will also abandon the fetters in the future; he has already severed the underlying tendencies and will also sever the underlying tendencies; he has already destroyed the outflows and will also destroy the outflows. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. These, monks, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Buddha then asked: "What four? Here, monks, one person is equal in head with respect to the past, equal in head with respect to the future, equal in head with respect to the present, and equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the past? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the five lower fetters (orambhāgiya-saṃyojana) in the past; he has already attained the fruit of stream-entry (sotāpatti-phala). This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the past. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the future? Here, monks, a certain person will abandon the five lower fetters in the future; he will attain the fruit of stream-entry. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the present? Here, monks, a certain person is abandoning the five lower fetters in the present; he is attaining the fruit of stream-entry. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the present. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the five lower fetters in the past and will also abandon the five lower fetters in the future; he has already attained the fruit of stream-entry and will also attain the fruit of stream-entry. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. These, monks, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Buddha then asked: "What four? Here, monks, one person is equal in head with respect to the past, equal in head with respect to the future, equal in head with respect to the present, and equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the past? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the three fetters (saṃyojana) and attenuated lust, hatred, and delusion in the past; he has already attained the fruit of once-returning (sakadāgāmiphala). This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the past. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the future? Here, monks, a certain person will abandon the three fetters and attenuate lust, hatred, and delusion in the future; he will attain the fruit of once-returning. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the present? Here, monks, a certain person is abandoning the three fetters and attenuating lust, hatred, and delusion in the present; he is attaining the fruit of once-returning. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the present. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the three fetters and attenuated lust, hatred, and delusion in the past and will also abandon the three fetters and attenuate lust, hatred, and delusion in the future; he has already attained the fruit of once-returning and will also attain the fruit of once-returning. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. These, monks, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Buddha then asked: "What four?

Here, monks, one person is equal in head with respect to the past, equal in head with respect to the future, equal in head with respect to the present, and equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the past? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the five lower fetters in the past; he has already attained the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphala). This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the past. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the future? Here, monks, a certain person will abandon the five lower fetters in the future; he will attain the fruit of non-returning. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the future. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to the present? Here, monks, a certain person is abandoning the five lower fetters in the present; he is attaining the fruit of non-returning. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to the present. And how, monks, is one a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future? Here, monks, a certain person has already abandoned the five lower fetters in the past and will also abandon the five lower fetters in the future; he has already attained the fruit of non-returning and will also attain the fruit of non-returning. This, monks, is called a person equal in head with respect to both the past and the future. These, monks, are the four kinds of
Wisdom regarding the right eradication and cessation of all phenomena, and their non-manifestation, is knowledge in the sense of having an even summit.
“Of all phenomena” means: the five aggregates, the twelve bases, the eighteen elements;
wholesome phenomena, unwholesome phenomena, indeterminate phenomena; phenomena of the sense sphere, phenomena of the fine-material sphere, and phenomena of the immaterial sphere.
Dhammas; dhammas not included [within the mundane].
One completely eradicates: through renunciation, one completely eradicates sensual desire; through non-ill will, one completely eradicates ill will;
through the perception of light, one completely eradicates sloth and torpor; through non-distraction, one [completely eradicates] restlessness.
One completely eradicates doubt through the discernment of phenomena; one completely eradicates ignorance through knowledge;
one completely eradicates discontent through gladness; one completely eradicates the hindrances through the first jhāna … and so on …
By means of the path of arahantship, one completely and rightly cuts off all defilements.
One brings about cessation: through renunciation, one brings about the cessation of sensual desire; through non-ill will, one brings about the cessation of ill will;

through the perception of light, one brings about the cessation of sloth and torpor; through non-distraction, one brings about the cessation of restlessness; and through the discernment of phenomena, one brings about the cessation of doubt.
He causes cessation: he causes ignorance to cease through knowledge; he causes discontent to cease through gladness;
he causes the hindrances to cease through the first jhāna … [and so on] … he causes all defilements to cease through the path of arahantship.
Non-appearance means that for one who has attained renunciation, sensual desire does not appear;
for one who has attained non-ill will, ill will does not appear; for one who has attained the perception of light, sloth and torpor do not appear;
for one who has attained non-distraction, restlessness does not appear; and for one who has attained the discernment of phenomena, doubt does not appear.
Ignorance does not arise for one who has attained knowledge; discontent does not arise for one who has attained gladness;
the hindrances do not arise for one who has attained the first jhāna;
…pe… all defilements do not arise for one who has attained the path of arahantship.
Because sensual desire has been abandoned, renunciation is even; because ill will has been abandoned, non-ill will is even;
because sloth and torpor have been abandoned, the perception of light is even; because restlessness has been abandoned, non-distraction is even;
because doubt has been abandoned, the discernment of phenomena is even; because ignorance has been abandoned, knowledge is even.

Because of the abandoning of discontent, gladness is even; because of the abandoning of the hindrances, the first jhāna is even … [and so on] … because of the abandoning of all defilements, the path of arahantship is even.
"Heads" refers to the thirteen heads.
Craving is the chief of obstacles; conceit is the chief of bondages; views are the chief of misapprehensions;
restlessness is the chief of distractions; ignorance is the chief of defilements; faith is the chief of resolve; energy is the chief of exertion;
mindfulness is the chief of establishment; concentration is the chief of non-distraction; wisdom is the chief of vision; and [volition] is the chief of occurrence.
The life-faculty is the head of its range, and liberation is the head of formations; cessation is the head of formations.
The Discussion on the Heads of Equal Length is finished.
